title: Introduce pre-defined perspectives
body:
Implements #1066.

**What this adds**

**1. Schema: three forms of a perspective, and `scopes` (cyclonedx-perspective-2.0.schema.json)**

A perspective is one of three mutually exclusive forms (oneOf, enforced in all directions):

```json
{ "bom-ref": "card-vision", "predefined": "cdx:perspectives:model-card", "predefinedVersion": 1, "scopes": [ … ] }
{ "bom-ref": "crypto-per-model", "ref": "def-crypto-in-use", "scopes": [ … ] }
{ "bom-ref": "custom", "name": "…", "mappings": [ … ], "scopes": [ … ] }
```

- **Pre-defined form** (`predefined` + `predefinedVersion`): incorporates a published perspective from the CycloneDX perspectives catalog by identity, giving tooling stable spec-backed identity instead of free-text name matching. Identities live under the reserved `cdx:` namespace with a `cdx:perspectives:` path (per @mrutkows), so they cannot collide with author-chosen names and can be declared in the reserved cyclonedx-property-taxonomy. `predefinedVersion` pins the published revision: it is the `version` of the catalog document defining the perspective (integer, incremented by 1 per revision, like other CycloneDX version fields). Initial identities: `cdx:perspectives:model-card` and `cdx:perspectives:pqc-readiness` (the latter reserved for the entry proposed in #960).
- **Definition reference form** (`ref`): applies a reusable inline perspective declared under `definitions.perspectives` (see 1b), by bom-ref or BOM-Link element.
- **Inline form** (`name` + `mappings`): fully defined in the document.

In the two reference forms only `bom-ref` and `scopes` may accompany the reference, so the referenced definition stays the single source of truth while the document decides where it applies.

**Why a field rather than the choice pattern.** A field on the perspective object keeps a pre-defined perspective addressable. A bare enum string cannot carry a bom-ref, so it could never be the target of a BOM-Link or any intra-document reference. With the field form, `{ "bom-ref": "…", "predefined": "cdx:perspectives:model-card", "predefinedVersion": 1 }` remains a first-class, referenceable node, and the oneOf enforces the same exclusivity the choice pattern would have.

**`scopes`: applying a perspective to parts of the document.** Without scopes a perspective applies to the whole document. With scopes, each entry is an independent application: one view, one completeness evaluation.

```json
"scopes": [
  { "bom-ref": "scope-vision", "name": "Vision model", "targets": ["model-vision"] },
  { "bom-ref": "scope-text",   "name": "Text models",
    "expressions": ["$.definitions.components[?(@.type=='machine-learning-model' && @.group=='text')]"] }
]
```

- `expressions[]`: JSONPath (RFC 9535) from the document root; `targets[]`: bom-ref or BOM-Link (`elementLink`, the type compositions use). At least one of the two; within a scope they union.
- Resolution (normative text on `scopes`, written as a numbered algorithm so implementations converge): (1) evaluate expressions from the root; (2) resolve targets by bom-ref; (3) one-hop closure: every same-document reference entry (an object with a `ref` property, as the inventory refactor introduces) inside the selected subtrees also selects the referenced node; (4) the scope is the union of the selected subtrees. Containment is by JSONPath Normalized Path prefix (RFC 9535 §2.7). BOM-Links to other documents are not followed.
- Mapping expressions stay root-absolute: a mapping selects the intersection of its expression with the scope. Nothing is relative, so catalog entries stay generic and the document decides where they apply. Published pre-defined perspectives and definitions declare no scopes of their own.
- Closure is tooling behaviour; the schema validates structure only.

**`via` on a mapping: following references.** JSONPath cannot join, so data *related* to a scoped subject (the datasets a model trained on, the risks that affect it, the algorithms a library provides) needed a way to be reached. `via` is an ordered list of traversal steps applied before the expression; each step is exactly one of:

- `{ "refs": "<root-absolute JSONPath>" }`: restricted to the current node set, collect reference values and resolve them to objects in this document. Forward references, e.g. a model's `training.datasets`.
- `{ "referrers": "<root-absolute JSONPath>" }`: the inverse. The path selects reference values anywhere in the document; the step produces the objects that hold a value identifying a node in the current set (the object owning the property, or, when the value sits in an array, the object holding the array). For relationships that point *towards* the scoped nodes, e.g. a risk's `affects`. The step replaces the current set with the matching referring objects; when the current set is the whole document it produces the whole document, so an unscoped perspective is not narrowed.
- `{ "dependencies": "depends-on" | "provides" | "dependents" | "provided-by", "transitive": bool }`: walk the dependency graph from the referenceable nodes within the current set.

The first step starts from the scope (or the whole document when unscoped); the expression is then intersected with the subtrees of what the last step produced. Steps chain:

```json
{ "expression": "$.definitions.components[?(@.type=='cryptographic-asset')]",
  "via": [ { "dependencies": "depends-on", "transitive": true }, { "dependencies": "provides" } ] }
```

Worked example for `referrers` (from @JunHwan-Kwon's review): two models, `risk-a` with `"affects": ["model-a"]`, `risk-b` with `"affects": ["model-b"]`. A model card scoped to `model-a` evaluates a risk mapping as: current set `{model-a}` → `referrers: $.risks.risks[*].affects[*]` yields `{risk-a}` → expression intersected with that subtree → `risk-a`. Unscoped, both risks are selected. Selection is automatic; authors do not add risks to the scope.

**1a. Registry: `schema/perspectives-defs.schema.json` + `schema/perspectives-defs.json`**

The identity enum does not live in the versioned perspective schema. It lives in a standalone registry at the schema root, which the perspective schema `$ref`s (`../../perspectives-defs.schema.json#/definitions/preDefinedPerspectivesEnum`), following the `cryptography-defs` pattern, so perspectives can be added or revised without a specification release.

- `perspectives-defs.schema.json` is hand-maintained: the identity enum (with `meta:enum` descriptions) plus the governing schema for the registry data. No mapping is declared; by naming convention the catalog document defining `cdx:perspectives:<name>` is `perspectives/<name>-perspective.json`.
- `perspectives-defs.json` is generated. Per identity it records every published version with the sha256 of the catalog document's canonical JSON and the commit that introduced it. Once registered, a version's content is immutable; changing a catalog document requires bumping its `version` by 1. Identities without a catalog document yet (`pqc-readiness`) are reserved and absent until their document lands.
- CI: the schema-v2 suite checks every identity on each PR (reserved, new, unchanged, or bumped by exactly one pass; a content change without a bump, a regressed or skipped version, or a removed registered document fail). A workflow runs the generator after merge and opens a PR registering any new version, mirroring `generate_algorithm_families.yml`.

**1b. Reusable definitions: `definitions.perspectives` (cyclonedx-definition-2.0.schema.json)**

Reusable inline perspectives, each with a required bom-ref, typed as `perspectiveDefinition`, a mixin over the perspective schema that forbids `predefined`, `predefinedVersion`, `ref` and `scopes`. The same definition can be applied at several places with different scopes without repeating its mappings. Follows the definitions-registry direction of #1075.

**2. Catalog: perspectives/model-card-perspective.json**

Second entry in the perspectives/ catalog introduced by #960, following its delivery shape (a complete, minimal, valid 2.0 document containing only the perspective). This is the definition incorporated when a document declares `"predefined": "cdx:perspectives:model-card"`. 23 mappings, eight reached through `via`:

- **Model identity**: details (name, version, description), identifiers (identity claims grouped by asserting party, e.g. a Package-URL for a model hub entry), supplier via party roles, licence.
- **Intrinsic characteristics** via `modelProperties`: tasks, learning types, architecture, inputs/outputs, size and quantization, evaluation, limitations, environmental considerations. Models are located by descendant search (`$..[?(@.type=='machine-learning-model')]`) so the entry applies whether models are declared at the document root, in inventories, or in definitions.
- **Training**: the training object; the training procedure reached through `via.refs` over `modelProperties.training.formula` into `$.formulation[*]` (workflows and tasks as the training stages and the data each consumed).
- **Datasets**, reached through `via.refs` over `modelProperties.training.datasets`, in four mappings so completeness can report which aspect is missing: identity and licensing (required), description and contents, classification and sensitive data, governance (parties accountable as owner, steward, custodian).
- **Intended use**: the model's use-case references, and the use-case definitions reached through `via.refs`; intended users via party roles.
- **Ethical and fairness considerations** as risk model entries (ethical domain; fairness/bias impact categories), reached through `via.referrers` over `$.risks.risks[*].affects[*]`: for a scoped model, exactly the risks that name it in `affects`; unscoped, every matching risk.

Not mappable today: provenance labels such as crawled or synthetic, and data subsets with rationale; the 2.0 data model has no fields for them.

**3. Tests**
- Fixtures (auto-discovered by the schema-v2 suite). Valid: the pre-defined reference form alongside a plain inline perspective; a scoped document exercising `targets`, `expressions`, a `definitions.perspectives` entry applied at two scopes by `ref`, a chained dependency traversal and a `refs` step; the two-models/two-risks document with a model card scoped to `model-a` and an inline perspective using `referrers`. Invalid: unknown identity (correct namespace, not in the enum); reference missing `predefinedVersion`; identity plus inline mappings; identity plus name and domains; scope with neither expressions nor targets; traversal step mixing `refs` and `dependencies`; traversal step mixing `referrers` and `refs`; unknown dependency direction; `ref` plus inline mappings; `ref` plus `predefined`; a definition declaring scopes; a definition without bom-ref.
- Registry test (`test:v2.0:t4-perspectives-registry`, runs in the JavaScript CI workflow on every PR): validates `perspectives-defs.json` against its governing schema, checks registered identities are in the enum with contiguous versions from 1 and conventional file paths, and assesses each identity's catalog document against the registry.
- Harness wiring: `perspectives-defs.schema.json` registered as an external schema in both JS ajv harnesses, the Java 2.x harness's classpath mapping, and the bundler's ref-exception list, mirroring `cryptography-defs.schema.json`.

**Not included**
- Bundled schemas — left to the post-merge bundle workflow, per repo convention.
- Conformance validation — the schema validates identity, exclusivity and structure; evaluating scopes, closure, traversal steps (`refs`, `referrers`, `dependencies`) and mapping expressions against a document's data remains tooling territory, as for perspectives generally. The fixtures pin the intended node selections in prose; a semantic evaluator would be a separate contribution.

**Dependencies**
- Premised on #990: the catalog entry's mappings target `modelProperties`, `training.datasets`, `training.formula` and `useCases`. The schema change and fixtures stand alone; only the catalog entry's JSONPath expressions assume #990's shape. Happy to adjust if that lands differently.
- Written with #1075 in mind: schema examples use the inventory layout, `definitions.perspectives` follows its definitions registry, and the catalog's descendant search covers both the current and the inventory layout. Fixtures keep the root `components` layout until #1075 lands.
- Complements #960: adopts its perspectives/ folder and delivery shape, and reserves `cdx:perspectives:pqc-readiness` for its entry; to be registered automatically, that document needs to live at `perspectives/pqc-readiness-perspective.json` at `version` 1.
